title: Pediatric Dosing: Weight Math + the Never List

questions.stem: A 5-year-old just had tonsil surgery. Is codeine an option for pain?

options.text: Never: it is on the never list

questions.explanation: C is correct: codeine is off-limits under 12, and under 18 after tonsil surgery, because fast metabolizers can stop breathing. A, B, and D ignore the danger.

questions.stem: A child weighs 44 pounds. What is the weight in kilograms?
questions.explanation: A is correct: 44 divided by 2.2 is 20 kilograms. B multiplies instead of dividing. C skips the conversion. D halves the right answer.

questions.stem: How should liquid medicines for children be measured?

options.text: With an oral syringe in milliliters

questions.explanation: C is correct: measure with an oral syringe in milliliters, never a kitchen spoon. A, B, and D invite dosing errors.

questions.stem: A 22 kg child needs acetaminophen 15 mg/kg using 160 mg per 5 mL liquid. About how many milliliters?
questions.explanation: B is correct: 22 times 15 is 330 mg, and 330 divided by 160, times 5, is about 10 mL. A is half the dose. C and D come from mixing up the numbers.

questions.stem: Which statements about children's fever medicines are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ibuprofen is only from 6 months of age
No aspirin in children or teens with viral illness
Aspirin is the first choice for children's fever
Acetaminophen dose is up to 15 mg/kg every 4 to 6 hours

questions.explanation: A, B, D, and E are correct as taught. C is wrong because aspirin can cause Reye syndrome.

questions.stem: Which items are on the never list? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tetracyclines under 8, except short doxycycline courses
Ceftriaxone plus intravenous calcium in newborns
Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines under 2

questions.explanation: A, B, C, and D are on the never list as taught. E is a normal acetaminophen dose.

questions.stem: Why are tetracyclines avoided under age 8?
questions.explanation: B is correct: tetracyclines stain growing teeth under 8. A is not taught for them. C is an aspirin risk. D is the ceftriaxone and calcium problem in newborns.

questions.stem: A 20 kg child needs high-dose amoxicillin at 90 mg/kg/day, split twice daily. What is each dose?
questions.explanation: D is correct: 20 times 90 is 1,800 mg per day, divided by 2 doses is 900 mg per dose. A is the whole day. B divides by 4. C is a tenfold error.

questions.stem: For a large teen, the weight-based calculation comes out above the adult dose. What should be given?
questions.explanation: B is correct: never exceed the adult maximum dose; it caps the weight math. A and C go past the adult maximum. D underdoses without reason.

questions.stem: Amoxicillin 900 mg per dose is needed, and the liquid is 400 mg per 5 mL. How many milliliters per dose?
questions.explanation: C is correct: 900 divided by 400, times 5, is 11.25 mL. A is the whole day's amount. B is half of one dose. D is double the full-day volume (22.5 × 2).
